paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jeroboam was afraid, and he said it only in his heart (1 Kings 12:26). Then he fixed his fear his own way instead of trusting the God who had given him the kingdom. Fear is loud, and it will hand you a plan that sounds smart at 2 AM.

Look at what his plan was built from. He made golden calves, appointed priests who were not Levites, and ordained a feast in "a month of his own choosing" (1 Kings 12:31-33). Everything looked like worship, but he built it to protect himself. The Bible says it plainly: "And this thing became a sin…" (1 Kings 12:30).

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. When worry shows up, take it to God before you take it to your own bright ideas. I've been scared in the dark myself, friend, and I'm so glad the answer wasn't something I cooked up on my own. And this story isn't over, so keep your oven warm.
